summary: A 1917 steel Aermotor lookout on Mount Tremper in the Catskills; closed 1971 or 1975, reopened 2001, and volunteers open the cab on weekends in season.

facts.design: 47-ft steel Aermotor LS-40 tower with 7x7-ft metal cab
facts.agency: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation

staffing.status: not fire-watch staffed; volunteers open the cab on weekends and holidays in season

access.note: Catskill Fire Tower Project volunteers open the cab Saturdays, Sundays and holiday Mondays, Memorial Day weekend through Indigenous Peoples Day weekend. Reached by a hike of about three miles from Plank Road in Phoenicia.

visit.trail_note: About three miles with roughly 2,000 ft of climbing from Plank Road in Phoenicia; the cab is open to visitors only on the volunteer days in season

events.note: Built by the New York Department of Conservation as a steel Aermotor tower; one hiking guide says it was first built elsewhere and moved
A 1930 newspaper describes an observer on watch from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m.
A 1955 newspaper notice records a new person appointed in charge of the tower
NHLR says the tower was in active service for 54 years and closed in 1971
HMDB marker says the tower was decommissioned in 1975; this conflicts with the NHLR's 1971 date
Registered April 28, 1997 per the NHLR record
Reopened after restoration by grassroots volunteers, the Catskill Center and NYS DEC
Added to the National Register of Historic Places as the Mount Tremper Fire Observation Station

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says the tower closed in 1971 after 54 years of service; the HMDB marker says it was decommissioned in 1975. The story gives both dates and does not pick one.
NHLR and Wikipedia give 47 ft (14.3 m); a 1917 newspaper item quoted by Forest Lookouts gives 65 ft. The record uses 14.3 m and the story notes the newspaper figure.

The Catskill Center says the 1917 tower is believed to be the original structure; Catskill Hiker says it was built elsewhere and moved. No source found confirms a move, so the story reports the claim as unconfirmed.

notes_for_editor: Dates and height conflict across sources (closure 1971 vs 1975; 47 ft vs 65 ft in a 1917 item). The Catskill Center page is undated, so staffing as_of is the year only. Andy Arthur pages returned HTTP 403 and were not used. The NHLR photo (Feb 2016, courtesy of Laurie Rankin) has no licence or URL, so no photo was added. The brief's access 'unknown' is now public based on the Catskill Center and marker.
